Compare word frequencies in explicit target and reference corpora

lexdiv_keyness.Rd

Retain corpus denominators, document-level counts and source occurrences beside descriptive G-squared and log-ratio scores. Return an exact term's occurrences to a source-aligned concordance without redefining the counted vocabulary.

Usage

lexdiv_keyness(x, target, reference, preprocessing_id,
    term_col = "surface", keep = rep(TRUE, nrow(x$tokens)), min_count = 1L,
    max_tokens = 1e6)
lexdiv_keyness_concordance(x, term, window = 5L, max_cells = 1e6)

Arguments

x

For comparison, an unchanged complete lexdiv_import_annotations result. For concordance, a complete unchanged keyness result, including a legacy keyness_compare() record.

target, reference

Nonempty vectors of unique known document IDs, with no ID shared between the two corpora. Other documents remain explicitly excluded.

preprocessing_id

Nonblank caller label for the chosen preprocessing and selection policy. It does not execute preprocessing or prove comparability.

term_col

Character token column to count using exact UTF-8 keys.

keep

One nonmissing logical value per original token. Missing/blank selected terms are unavailable and retained in coverage accounting.

min_count

Positive whole pooled-count threshold, returned as a flag only. It does not change the vocabulary, background counts or denominator.

max_tokens

Positive whole-number bound on original input token rows.

term

One exact term present in the saved comparison.

window, max_cells

Context width and allocation bound passed to lexdiv_concordance.

Details

Vocabulary is the union of counted terms in both corpora. Each denominator is all counted tokens in that corpus. Two-by-two cells are term and other-token counts. G-squared is 2 * sum(O * log(O/E)), with zero observed-cell contributions zero and no continuity correction. Signed G-squared uses the direction of the rate difference; log-ratio is the base-2 logarithm of the target rate divided by the reference rate, without smoothing. An observed zero produces an infinite log-ratio; an empty corpus produces missing scores with reasons. Document counts and missing terms remain distinct from pooled token counts.

These are descriptive scores, not p-values, significance decisions or measures of writer proficiency. Corpus representativeness, writer/task dependence and multiple testing require separate research decisions. Identical source-text sequences across groups are flagged; near duplicates are not detected.

Counting requires no optional package. Returning to KWIC uses optional quanteda (>= 4.5.0) and restricts endpoints to the exact counted term before matching, preserving Unicode key distinctions. Source text is retained in the complete result. Legacy examples/keyness.R still defines its old names and output shapes. See keyness comparison guide.

Value

lexdiv_keyness() returns a plain list with results (two-by-two cells, totals, expected cells, per-1000 rates, log-ratio, G-squared, signed G-squared, direction, document frequencies, threshold flag and status), totals, documents, document_counts, occurrences, token_audit, complete source, settings, provenance and integrity_sha256. Absent document-term rows in the sparse document_counts table must be interpreted with document coverage.

lexdiv_keyness_concordance() returns comparison_id, term and search, a lexdiv_concordance result usable with plot().

Examples

segments <- data.frame(document_id = c("target", "reference"), segment_id = "s1",
  text = c("a a b", "a b b"))
tokens <- data.frame(document_id = rep(segments$document_id, each = 3),
  segment_id = "s1", token_index = rep(1:3, 2), surface = c("a", "a", "b", "a", "b", "b"))
source <- lexdiv_import_annotations(tokens, segments, list(language = "en",
  analyzer = "authored", analyzer_version = "1", dictionary = "none",
  dictionary_version = "none", unit = "supplied tokens", normalization = "none"))
comparison <- lexdiv_keyness(source, "target", "reference", "surface-all")
comparison$results[c("term", "target_count", "reference_count", "log_ratio")]
#>   term target_count reference_count log_ratio
#> 1    a            2               1         1
#> 2    b            1               2        -1
if (requireNamespace("quanteda", quietly = TRUE)) {
  evidence <- lexdiv_keyness_concordance(comparison, "a")
  evidence$search$occurrences
}
#>   query_id document_id segment_id from to document_from document_to start end
#> 1  feature      target         s1    1  1             1           1     1   1
#> 2  feature      target         s1    2  2             2           2     3   3
#> 3  feature   reference         s1    1  1             1           1     1   1
#>   pre keyword post matched_terms left_tokens right_tokens
#> 1           a  a b             a                     a, b
#> 2  a        a    b             a           a            b
#> 3           a  b b             a                     b, b
#>                                                      occurrence_id
#> 1 4ec6c37193104e90e9166d30bccd65daedde5cc5366753be792bbde5eba7c685
#> 2 51944ee3acabdfe00295d12799ccef0890f25477ad2ed84781c1004f2d6967b0
#> 3 d1b9abecf37571c303a07a04a4be6f02d73d1e8e16b29d8a66ac7043ad906ae9
